title: I've been building a dark fantasy idle RPG in Godot 4 using Codex and AI-generated artwork
author: Knuckleclot
selftext:
I've been working on Fellvault, a dark fantasy idle RPG for mobile, and wanted to share how far I've gotten using AI-assisted development.

I'm a software developer, but this is my first serious attempt at building a mobile RPG in Godot.

I've been using Codex heavily for GDScript implementation, while handling the gameplay direction, progression systems, balancing, testing and iteration myself.

Generative AI has also been a big part of creating the game's characters, environments and equipment artwork. Getting everything to feel consistent inside one game has required quite a bit of iteration.

The game itself has automatic combat, optional tapping, Fury attacks, dungeon bosses, equipment drops, and a forge for enhancing and evolving gear.

The clip shows the current gameplay running in Godot 4.

For transparency, AI has also helped with some text and planning. Sound effects were created programmatically using Godot, without generative AI.

I'm preparing the first external iOS beta, with Android testing planned too.

I'm curious how other developers using AI are handling the transition from generating individual assets and features to getting everything polished and consistent in an actual game.
